route_summary: 22,000 + 3,000 random starts by two independent implementations found no four MU bases in C^6; ~71% converge to L = 0.0512492189962838 (ASD 0.99829169), a rediscovery of the published Raynal-Lu-Englert optimum. Controls: d=2 floor 2/3 proved; known MU sets in d=3,4,5,7 and three bases in d=6 are all found.

attempts.range: 22,000 random starts of projected-gradient descent on 4 bases of C^6 (seeds 7 and 20261002, 50,000-iteration cap); controls d=2..7 under identical settings
attempts.one_line: No four MU bases in C^6 across 22,000 random starts; the dominant endpoint (70.7%) reproduces the published four-basis optimum ASD 0.99829, with every residual defect between the three Hadamard bases.
gaps: Floor not certified as a local (let alone global) minimum.
Local search cannot exclude a narrow basin: the d=7 control finds known complete sets in only 0.7% of starts.

attempts.range: 001's claims about the d=6, k=4 floor value, its share of starts, its basis structure and overlap pattern, and the d=2,3,5 and d=6,k=3 controls; checked by an independent exponential-map L-BFGS implementation over 3,000 d=6,k=4 starts
attempts.one_line: Independent exponential-map L-BFGS code reproduces 001's floor L = 0.0512492189962838 (71.6% of starts), its structure and its controls, with no corrections; the same value is also a 3-basis local minimum.
